sentences.Monica har fått vondt i ryggen og har so: Monica has a bad back and has slept badly all night.
sentences.Hun kan nesten ikke gå om morgenen, og h: She can hardly walk in the morning, and she realises she won't manage to go to work.
sentences.Derfor ringer hun til jobben for å gi be: So she calls work to let them know.
sentences.I resepsjonen sitter Torstein, som er en: At reception sits Torstein, who is a good colleague of Monica's.
Listen, I can't come to work today.
sentences.Jeg har vondt i ryggen og kan nesten ikk: My back hurts and I can hardly walk.
sentences.Å det var synd! Stakkars deg!: Oh, that's a shame! You poor thing!
sentences.Har du vært hos legen?: Have you been to the doctor?
sentences.Nei, ikke ennå. Jeg håper jeg blir bedre: No, not yet. I hope I'll be better tomorrow.
sentences.Kan du si fra til ham når du ser ham?: Can you tell him when you see him?
Yes, of course. I'll let him know.
sentences.Takk skal du ha. Jeg ringer i morgen hvi: Thank you. I'll call tomorrow if I'm just as bad.
sentences.Torstein har også tatt imot to andre bes: Torstein has also taken two other messages for Larsen:
sentences.Emne: Dale kommer senere i dag: Subject: Dale is coming in later today
Dale is coming after twelve. Sick child.
sentences.Barnehagen ringte. Ellen har feber og ka: The kindergarten called. Ellen has a temperature and is throwing up.
Pick her up as soon as possible.
